name: F1 constructors at Monza
description:
The same ten F1 teams as at Yas, about 1.5 s a lap apart at the limit. Monza is long straights and slow chicanes, so low drag pays: Helix and Saltire close right up, and Ferro's weak engine drops it to the back with Ember. Each team below, fastest first, with its gap to Meridian per lap.
- Meridian (Abreu, Alvarez): best overall: never the best in any one part of the lap, never far off it. The benchmark.
- Aurora (Dlamini, Bianchi): the most downforce: best in fast corners, second-best brakes, 5 km/h down on top speed. +0.18 s.
- Helix (Kowalski, Hughes): the lowest drag (348 km/h), loses time braking and in the corners. +0.50 s.
- Saltire (Petrov, Nakamura): low drag (346 km/h) and the least grip in the midfield. +0.61 s.
- Brightwater (Laurent, Jovanovic): the strongest engine: quickest out of slow corners and down the straights, weaker in the braking zones. +0.63 s.
- Kestrel (Chen, Fontaine): the most mechanical grip: best in slow corners, good brakes, slow on the straights. +0.66 s.
- Corsair (Eriksen, Ito): the best brakes, ordinary everywhere else. +0.69 s.
- Lumen (Olsen, Murphy): no strength and no weakness, a step down everywhere. +0.95 s.
- Ember (Schmidt, Reyes): the least downforce and grip in the field, an average engine. +1.46 s.
- Ferro (Quinn, Garcia): strong brakes and grip but the weakest engine (336 km/h). +1.48 s.
Better drivers mostly at the better teams, not strictly. Qualifying sets the grid; ten laps.
